newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to report to Congress on Mexico drugs.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to report to Congress on Mexico drugs.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has agreed to a Senate request for a report on the progress Mexico is making combating drugs and drug cartels, a decision welcomed on Friday by the Senators who sought it.

Angered by the administration's certification last February of Mexico as an ally in the war on drugs, the House and Senate passed separate bills. The House backed decertifying Mexico. The Senate did not go that far, but it did demand an administration report by September on whether Mexico was strengthening its anti-drug efforts.

Georgia Republican Paul Coverdell and California Democrat Dianne Feinstein, sponsors of the bipartisan Senate measure, thanked Clinton for complying with the request, which never had the force of law. Clinton agreed in a letter dated May 14, and made public by the senators on Friday.

The senators demanded that the report cover areas including Mexico's action against drug cartels, whether Mexico complies with any of the 13 outstanding extradition requests from the United States and implementation and enforcement of new money-laundering laws.
It also will include an assessment of whether the newly-created anti-drugs office is less corrupt than the notoriously venal National Institute for Combating Drugs that it replaced.
"It is a new platform, it is an acknowledgement of the issues (we) were trying to bring before the Congress, the nation and the people of Mexico," said Coverdell.

"I believe that the drug war in our hemisphere could potentially destabilize the hemisphere, is doing enormous damage to the youth of our country and is an issue that must receive far more attention than it has today," he said.
Feinstein said the report "would be an important indicator of whether Mexico has taken the decision to approach this terrible problem in a cooperative partnership and a full way."

"Unless the report can cite significant and demonstrable progress in cooperation, the answer very sadly will be that Mexico has not yet taken such a decision. I hope that not be the case on September 1," she said.
